schema_ddl:
CREATE TABLE R1 (A INT, B INT);
CREATE TABLE R2 (A INT, B INT);
q1: SELECT X.B AS XB, Y.B AS YB FROM R1 AS X, R2 AS Y
q2: SELECT X1.XB AS XB, Y1.YB AS YB FROM (SELECT X.B AS XB FROM R1 AS X) AS X1, (SELECT Y.B AS YB FROM R2 AS Y) AS Y1
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT X.B AS XB, Y.B AS YB FROM R1 AS X, R2 AS Y
q2_prompt_sql: SELECT X1.XB AS XB, Y1.YB AS YB FROM (SELECT X.B AS XB FROM R1 AS X) AS X1, (SELECT Y.B AS YB FROM R2 AS Y) AS Y1
counterexample: INSERT INTO R1 (A, B) VALUES (1, NULL), (2, 2); INSERT INTO R2 (A, B) VALUES (3, 3), (4, NULL);
explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not semantically equivalent because Q1 performs a Cartesian product between R1 and R2, while Q2 first projects R1 and R2 into subqueries X1 and Y1, respectively, and then performs a Cartesian product between these subqueries. This difference in the order of operations can lead to different results if the tables R1 and R2 have NULL values.
counterexample_dsp: The test data should have NULL values in the B column of at least one of the tables to trigger the difference in results between Q1 and Q2.
